dishes.name: Pesarattu
dishes.description: Pesarattu is a traditional breakfast dish of Andhra Pradesh, made mainly from whole green gram, cooked without fermentation and served with spicy Allam Pachadi.
dishes.keyTechnique: Stone-Ground Unfermented Batter & Cast Iron Tawa Roasting

dishes.name: Avakaya
dishes.description: Avakaya is a traditional raw-mango pickle from Andhra Pradesh, preserved in mustard powder, red chilli, and cold-pressed gingelly oil.
ingredients: Black chickpeas (optional, in place of garlic)
Hot rice with dal and ghee for serving
dishes.keyTechnique: Raw-Mango Sun-Dried Spice Curing & Gingelly Oil Maceration

dishes.name: Thukpa
dishes.description: Hearty handmade wheat noodles steeped in a warming clear broth infused with indigenous mountain herbs, ginger, garlic, and wild greens.
dishes.keyTechnique: Clear Broth Infusion & Clay Pot Simmering

dishes.name: Bamboo Shoot Pork
dishes.description: Tender country pork slow-cooked with fresh shredded bamboo shoots, King Chillies, and indigenous wild mountain coriander in bamboo hollows.
dishes.keyTechnique: Flame Roasting Inside Green Bamboo Internodes

dishes.name: Apong
dishes.alternateName: Rice Beer of the Adi and Nyishi
dishes.description: A lightly effervescent rice beer brewed from fermented rice and a herbal starter cake, strained and diluted with water; central to Adi and Nyishi hospitality, festivals and communal labour.
dishes.era: Indigenous fermentation tradition; documented in ethnographic accounts, not in a dated recipe
dishes.keyTechnique: Starter-Cake Fermentation & Bamboo Straining

dishes.name: Masor Tenga
dishes.description: A bright, light, golden fish broth made sour with fresh tomatoes and ou tenga (elephant apple), tempered gently in pure pungent cold-pressed mustard oil.
dishes.keyTechnique: Minimal Oil Tempering & Natural Acid Simmer

dishes.name: Khar
dishes.description: A ceremonial starter prepared by filtering water through the ash of sun-dried sun-charred Bhim banana peels, simmered with raw papaya and mustard oil.
dishes.keyTechnique: Sun-Dry Peeling, Charcoal Leaching & Slow Emulsification

dishes.name: Til Pitha
dishes.description: A thin rice-flour pancake dry-roasted on a hot tawa, rolled around a filling of toasted black sesame and jaggery, and made in quantity for Magh Bihu and Bohag Bihu.
dishes.era: Bihu harvest tradition; documented in Assamese household and festival cookery
dishes.keyTechnique: Dry-Tawa Rice Crepe & Sesame-Jaggery Rolling

dishes.name: Litti Chokha
dishes.description: Rustic whole-wheat dough spheres stuffed with spiced roasted Bengal gram flour (sattu), baked over cow-dung ember fires and dipped in golden cow ghee, served with smoked brinjal chokha.
dishes.keyTechnique: Cow-Dung Wood Ember Baking & Ghee Immersion

dishes.name: Thekua
dishes.description: Sacred crisp wheat cookies patterned on carved wooden moulds (saancha), sweetened with date jaggery, scented with crushed green cardamom and fennel, deep-fried in pure ghee.
dishes.keyTechnique: Wood Saancha Embossing & Deep Ghee Confection

dishes.name: Silao Khaja
dishes.description: Paper-thin layers of wheat-flour dough, folded repeatedly with ghee, deep-fried until crisp and saturated with sugar syrup; the layered sweet of Silao near Nalanda, now GI-registered.
dishes.era: Silao sweet-making tradition, documented in 20th-century regional accounts and the GI Registry
dishes.keyTechnique: Repeated Lamination, Frying & Syrup Saturation

dishes.name: Chila
dishes.description: Thin, crispy golden crepes made from indigenous Chhattisgarh rice batter, sprinkled with roasted sesame and served with fiery green tomato coriander chutney.
dishes.keyTechnique: Clay Tawa Roasting with Sesame Crust

dishes.name: Fara
dishes.description: Crescent-shaped steamed dumplings made from fresh rice flour stuffed with a spicy chana dal and garlic herb paste, lightly pan-tossed in mustard and curry leaves.
dishes.keyTechnique: Clay Steaming & Crisp Pan Tempering

dishes.name: Bafauri
dishes.description: Spiced gram-flour dumplings steamed until firm, then sliced and tempered with mustard, curry leaves and green chilli — a protein-rich, oil-light dish from Chhattisgarhi home kitchens.
dishes.era: Regional household technique; no securely dated first written reference
dishes.keyTechnique: Besan Batter Steaming & Post-Steam Tempering

dishes.name: Goan Fish Curry
dishes.description: Fresh coastal kingfish or mackerel simmered in freshly extracted thick coconut milk, brightened by tart sun-dried kokum rinds and fiery Kashmiri chillies.
dishes.keyTechnique: Clay Pot Simmering & Stone Ground Masala

dishes.name: Pork Vindaloo
dishes.description: A masterwork of Indo-Portuguese culinary fusion: pork marinated overnight in palm toddy vinegar, garlic cloves, cinnamon, and fiery dried red chillies.
dishes.keyTechnique: Toddy Vinegar Acid Cure & Slow Copper Pot Braise

dishes.name: Bebinca
dishes.description: Seven (or more) thin coconut-milk, egg-yolk and flour layers, each grilled or baked before the next is poured, finished with a glossy top layer and cut in diamond slices.
dishes.era: Indo-Portuguese Goan baking tradition, documented in 20th-century Goan cookery
dishes.keyTechnique: Sequential Layer Baking Under Grill Heat

dishes.name: Dhokla
dishes.description: Porous, pillow-soft steamed savoury sponge cakes made from fermented split chickpea batter, tempered with crackling mustard seeds, green chillies, and fresh coriander.
dishes.keyTechnique: Aerated Fermentation & Steam Vapor Lift

dishes.name: Undhiyu
dishes.description: Surat's legendary winter one-pot casserole of tender baby eggplants, purple yam, Surti papdi beans, and fenugreek muthias slow-cooked upside down under earthen pit fires.
dishes.keyTechnique: Matka Inversion (Undhu) Under Charcoal Embers

dishes.name: Bajra Khichdi
dishes.description: Nutritious whole pearl millet pounded in stone mortars, simmered for hours with yellow moong lentils and crowned with a generous pool of freshly churned white butter.
dishes.keyTechnique: Mortar De-husking & Slow Earthen Pot Hearth Simmer

dishes.name: Kadhi Pakora
dishes.description: A golden, tangy stew of churned sour buttermilk and chickpea flour slow-simmered with fenugreek seeds, holding crisp onion-spinach pakoras, topped with ghee tadka.
dishes.keyTechnique: Prolonged Simmering (Kadhna) to Prevent Curdling

dishes.name: Haryanvi Churma
dishes.description: Coarse wheat-flour rotis baked over a cow-dung-fired hearth, crushed by hand and kneaded with desi ghee and jaggery or sugar; traditionally eaten with bajra roti, milk and seasonal greens.
dishes.era: Agrarian Haryanvi food tradition; documented in regional food writing
dishes.keyTechnique: Hearth-Baked Roti Crushing & Ghee Binding

dishes.name: Siddu
dishes.description: A pillowy, crescent-shaped fermented wheat dough bread filled with a rich paste of toasted local walnuts, poppy seeds, and wild herbs, drenched in hot desi ghee.
dishes.keyTechnique: Yeast Fermentation & Alpine Herbal Steaming

dishes.name: Himachali Dham
dishes.description: A ceremonial sattvic temple banquet cooked exclusively by hereditary 'Botis' in heavy brass degs, starring slow-simmered rajma madra cooked in rich spiced curd and dried fruits.
dishes.keyTechnique: Wood-Fire Brass Deg Simmering Without Onion-Garlic

dishes.name: Chana Madra
dishes.description: Chickpeas simmered in a whisked yoghurt and gram-flour gravy with ghee, cumin and asafoetida, thickened slowly without a tomato base; the centrepiece of a Chamba–Kangra Dham feast.
dishes.era: Himachali Dham tradition; documented in regional festival cookery
dishes.keyTechnique: Slow Yoghurt Gravy Simmering Without Curdling

dishes.name: Dhuska
dishes.description: Deep-golden crispy pancakes prepared by soaking and grinding short-grain rice and chana dal into a thick batter, fried in mustard oil and served with spicy aloo-chana sabzi.
dishes.keyTechnique: Wet-Stone Grinding & Rapid Immersion Frying

dishes.name: Chilka Roti
dishes.description: Traditional delicate tribal flatbreads prepared from coarse unpolished red rice and chana dal batter, poured on earthen tawas greased with sal leaf twigs.
dishes.keyTechnique: Earthen Tawa Pouring with Botanical Swab

dishes.name: Pittha
dishes.description: Rice-flour dough shaped by hand into crescents or cups, sometimes filled with jaggery and sesame, steamed over a cloth-lined pot and eaten at harvest festivals across Jharkhand's tribal communities.
dishes.era: Tribal harvest-festival tradition; documented in ethnographic and regional accounts
dishes.keyTechnique: Hand-Shaped Rice Dough & Cloth Steaming

dishes.name: Masala Dosa
dishes.description: World-renowned golden crisp fermented rice and black gram crepe, smeared inside with red garlic-chilli chutney, rolled around spiced potato palya, served on a green banana leaf.
dishes.keyTechnique: Stone-Ground Natural Fermentation & Iron Tawa Crisp-Folding

dishes.name: Bisi Bele Bath
dishes.description: A comforting royal Mysore palace preparation of short-grain rice, toor dal, tamarind extract, and 30-spice bisi bele powder, enriched with fried cashews and pure ghee.
dishes.era: Wodeyar Dynasty (16th Century CE Mysore Court)
dishes.keyTechnique: Layered Spice Roasting & Unified One-Pot Ghee Simmer

dishes.name: Appam with Vegetable Stew
dishes.description: Bowl-shaped fermented rice hoppers with gossamer lacy edges and soft, spongy steamed centers, paired with a fragrant coconut milk stew perfumed with green peppercorn and cinnamon.
dishes.era: 1st Century CE Syrian Christian & Malabar Maritime Heritage
dishes.keyTechnique: Deep Appachatti Swirl & Dual Coconut Milk Extraction

dishes.name: Kerala Fish Molee
dishes.description: Tender Karimeen (pearl spot) fish fillets gently poached in silky fresh coconut milk, golden turmeric, mild green chillies, and curry leaves with zero heavy browning.
dishes.keyTechnique: Delicate Fish Poach in Layered Coconut Milk Presses

dishes.name: Puttu
dishes.description: Cylinders of coarsely moistened rice flour and grated coconut steamed in a two-part puttu kutti, eaten hot with kadala curry, banana or a spoon of sugar.
dishes.era: Sangam-era Kerala & Tamil kitchen continuity (tradition; no securely dated first reference)
dishes.keyTechnique: Puttu Kutti Steam-Column Layering

dishes.name: Indori Poha
dishes.description: Fragrant flattened rice steamed over water pots, tempered with fennel seeds and turmeric, crowned with crispy Ratlami sev, pomegranate jewels, and jeeravan spice powder.
ingredients: Ratlami or Indori sev, and masala boondi (nukti)
dishes.keyTechnique: Steam-Pot Hydration & Jeeravan Masala Dusting

dishes.name: Bhutte Ka Kees
dishes.description: Tender sweet corn kernels grated fresh and slow-cooked in full-cream milk with asafoetida, green chillies, and mustard, garnished with fresh coconut and lemon.
ingredients: Lemon (for tang) and jeeravan masala / sev (optional)
dishes.keyTechnique: Fine Grating & Slow Milk-Emulsion Braise

dishes.name: Dal Bafla
dishes.description: Wheat-flour balls boiled first and then baked until blistered — unlike a dry baati — cracked open, drenched in ghee and served with a slow-cooked panchmel dal from the Malwa and Bundelkhand regions.
ingredients: Turmeric powder and pinch of baking soda
Panchmel dal (toor, chana, moong, urad, masoor)
Spicy red garlic chutney & lemon wedges
dishes.era: Malwa–Bundelkhand household tradition; documented in regional cookery
dishes.keyTechnique: Boil-Then-Bake Wheat Dumpling

dishes.name: Vada Pav
dishes.description: Golden spiced mashed potato ball encased in a crisp chickpea batter shell, tucked inside a fresh bakery pav slathered with fiery dry garlic-peanut chutney and green chilli.
dishes.era: 1966 CE (Dadar Station Creation by Ashok Vaidya)
dishes.keyTechnique: Tempered Potato Mash & Precision Deep Frying

dishes.name: Puran Poli
dishes.description: Paper-thin festive wheat flatbread rolled with a decadent core of slow-cooked Bengal gram and organic jaggery perfumed with nutmeg and cardamom, griddled with pure ghee.
dishes.keyTechnique: Puran Stone-Straining & Translucent Rolling

dishes.name: Eromba
dishes.description: Iconic Meitei dish of boiled mountain potatoes, tree beans (yongchak), and water greens mashed with toasted sun-dried fermented fish (ngari) and fiery king chillies.
dishes.keyTechnique: Dry Earthen Pot Roasting of Ngari & Hand Mashing

dishes.name: Singju
dishes.description: A fiery raw tribal salad featuring crunchy lotus stems, shredded cabbage, and seasonal herbs tossed with roasted black sesame, perilla seeds, and toasted ngari.
dishes.keyTechnique: Raw Julian Chiffonade & Dry Seed Dressing

dishes.name: Chak-Hao Kheer
dishes.description: A slow-cooked pudding of aromatic Manipuri black rice (Chak-Hao), milk and jaggery or sugar, served at feasts and now protected by the Chak-Hao geographical indication.
dishes.era: Manipuri rice-cultivation tradition; Chak-Hao registered as a GI in 2020
dishes.keyTechnique: Long Soak & Low-Heat Black-Rice Reduction

dishes.name: Jadoh
dishes.description: The revered ceremonial centrepiece of Khasi celebrations: aromatic indigenous short red hill rice cooked with succulent cuts of pork, ginger paste, and toasted black sesame.
dishes.keyTechnique: Rendered Pork Fat Rice Braising & Sesame Glaze

dishes.name: Dohneiiong
dishes.description: Tender pork cubes braised in a dark, thick paste made from stone-ground roasted black sesame seeds (neiiong), mountain ginger, and garlic with earthy mineral depths.
dishes.keyTechnique: Dry Seed Roasting, Stone Pounding & Long Braise

dishes.name: Pumaloi
dishes.description: Coarsely ground rice moistened and steamed in a special earthen or metal steamer (siew) until it rises into a light crumb; a Khasi ceremonial food served with meat or tea.
dishes.era: Khasi ceremonial food tradition; documented in ethnographic accounts
dishes.keyTechnique: Coarse Rice Meal Steaming in a Siew

dishes.name: Mizo Bai
dishes.description: The soul of Mizo daily sustenance: a completely oil-free clear soup made by simmering mountain greens, pork rind, and fresh fermented bamboo shoots in alkaline water.
dishes.keyTechnique: Oil-Free Alkaline Water Simmering

dishes.name: Sawhchiar
dishes.description: A thick, comforting highland rice porridge slow-cooked with bone-in chicken or country pork, seasoned simply with crushed ginger root, garlic, and wild black pepper.
dishes.keyTechnique: Continuous Wood-Fire Stirring to Creamy Rice Gel

dishes.name: Vawksa Rep
dishes.description: Pork smoked over the kitchen hearth, then simmered with bamboo shoot, local herbs and chilli; a Mizo staple that turns preservation into a distinct flavour.
dishes.era: Mizo hearth-preservation tradition; documented in regional food writing
dishes.keyTechnique: Hearth Smoking & Slow Bamboo-Shoot Braise

dishes.name: Naga Smoked Pork with Bamboo Shoots
dishes.description: Wood-hearth smoked pork cured over kitchen rafters for weeks, stewed with sour fermented bamboo shoots (bastenga) and fresh Naga King Chillies (Bhut Jolokia).
dishes.keyTechnique: Multi-Week Kitchen Hearth Smoking & Water Braise

dishes.name: Galho
dishes.description: A wholesome one-pot porridge of broken local hill rice, smoked pork cuts, seasonal wild greens, and pungent fermented soybeans (axone) lending rich umami.
dishes.keyTechnique: Slow Simmering with Fermented Bean Emulsification

dishes.name: Zutho
dishes.description: A milky, mildly sour fermented rice drink of the Angami Nagas, prepared from sprouted rice and a local starter, diluted and served in bamboo tumblers at communal work and festivals.
dishes.era: Angami fermentation tradition; documented in ethnographic accounts
dishes.keyTechnique: Sprouted-Rice Starter Fermentation & Dilution

dishes.name: Dalma
dishes.description: The sacred soul food of Odisha and Puri Jagannath temple: toor dal simmered with native country vegetables, tempered with panch phoron, dried red chillies, and pure desi ghee, and crowned with freshly grated coconut and roasted cumin-chilli powder.
dishes.keyTechnique: Earthen Kudua Pot Steam Layering & Ghee Chhunka

dishes.name: Chhena Poda
dishes.description: Chenna Poda originated in Nayagarh, Odisha, traditionally made using fresh cottage cheese, sugar and semolina, slowly baked to achieve its distinctive caramelized crust and traditional flavour.
dishes.keyTechnique: Controlled Earthen & Oven Baking Caramelization

dishes.name: Pakhala Bhata
dishes.description: A refreshing traditional Odia rice dish made by soaking cooked rice in water, often naturally fermented and served with curd, green chillies and local accompaniments.
dishes.keyTechnique: Natural Rice Fermentation & Mustard Oil Chhunka

dishes.name: Makki di Roti & Sarson da Saag
dishes.description: Stone-ground yellow cornmeal flatbreads patted by hand, paired with winter mustard and bathua greens slow-churned for hours with corn flour, finished with a melting mountain of fresh white butter.
ingredients: Fresh ginger, garlic and green chillies
dishes.keyTechnique: Clay Pot Churning (Ghotna) & Hand-Patted Tawa Griddling

dishes.name: Butter Chicken
dishes.description: Tandoor-charred succulent chicken pieces gently simmered in a velvety, silk-smooth gravy of strained ripe tomatoes, churned butter, fresh cream, and fragrant dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi).
ingredients: Kashmiri red chilli powder and turmeric
Salt and a pinch of sugar
dishes.keyTechnique: Clay Tandoor Roasting & Silky Tomato-Butter Emulsion

dishes.name: Amritsari Kulcha
dishes.description: A stuffed bread of refined wheat flour, layered with ghee and spiced potato or paneer, slapped into a tandoor wall until it blisters, then crushed with white butter and served with chole.
ingredients: Ghee or butter (for lamination and topping)
dishes.era: Amritsar tandoor culture, documented in 20th-century food writing
dishes.keyTechnique: Tandoor-Charged Stuffed Kulcha Baking

dishes.name: Dal Baati Churma
dishes.description: Hard wheat dumplings baked over dried cow-dung embers and cracked open into pools of piping hot ghee, paired with five-lentil panchmel dal and sweet powdered wheat churma.
dishes.keyTechnique: Sand / Ember Baking & Saturated Ghee Dunking

dishes.name: Laal Maas
dishes.description: The fiery crown jewel of Rajput royal hunting expeditions: game meat slow-cooked in pure ghee with an abundance of smoky Mathania red chillies, garlic paste, and crushed spices.
dishes.keyTechnique: Slow Ghee Braise & Mathania Chilli Extraction

dishes.name: Ghewar
dishes.description: A lacy, honeycombed disc made by pouring a thin flour-and-ghee batter into hot ghee in concentric rings, then drenched in sugar syrup and often finished with rabri; a Teej and Raksha Bandhan sweet.
dishes.era: Rajasthani monsoon-festival sweet, documented in 20th-century sweet-making accounts
dishes.keyTechnique: Ring-Poured Batter Frying & Syrup Soaking

dishes.name: Sikkimese Momos
dishes.description: Delicate pleated parcels of hand-rolled dough filled with seasoned pork mince or mountain vegetables and ginger, steamed over boiling herb water, served with fiery dalle khursani dip.
dishes.keyTechnique: Thin Pleated Pinching & Tiered Aluminium/Bamboo Steaming

dishes.name: Gundruk Soup
dishes.description: Sun-dried fermented mustard and radish leaves slow-simmered with tomatoes, green chillies, and ginger into a sour, mineral-dense curative alpine soup.
dishes.keyTechnique: Earthen Jar Fermentation, Sun Dehydration & Clear Broth Boil

dishes.name: Sel Roti
dishes.description: A ring-shaped, slightly sweet bread from a poured rice-flour and banana batter, deep-fried in a wide karahi and made for Tihar, Dashain and Sikkimese Nepali weddings.
dishes.era: Nepali–Sikkimese festival tradition; documented in regional food writing
dishes.keyTechnique: Poured-Ring Batter Frying

dishes.name: Chettinad Chicken Curry
dishes.description: An intoxicatingly aromatic curry from the wealthy mercantile Nattukotai Chettiars, prepared with 18 freshly stone-roasted spices including black stone flower (kalpasi), star anise, and peppercorns.
dishes.keyTechnique: Whole Spice Dry Roasting & Heavy Cast Bronze Uruli Simmer

dishes.name: Idli Sambar
dishes.description: Cloud-soft steamed pillows of fermented rice and dehusked black gram batter, submerged in a fragrant, piping hot toor dal stew simmered with shallots, drumsticks, and tamarind.
dishes.keyTechnique: Wet Stone Grinding, Overnight Aeration & Wet Cloth Steaming

dishes.name: Filter Coffee
dishes.description: A two-tier steel filter drips a dark coffee-chicory decoction overnight; it is cut with boiling milk and pulled between a dabarah and tumbler until a crown of froth forms.
dishes.era: Madras coffee-house culture, documented from the early 20th century
dishes.keyTechnique: Two-Tier Drip Filter & Dabarah Frothing

dishes.name: Hyderabadi Dum Biryani
dishes.description: The undisputed monarch of Indian culinary art: raw spiced marinated meat layered with 70% parboiled aged basmati rice, saffron milk, and caramelized onions, sealed in a handi with dough and slow-cooked over wood embers.
dishes.keyTechnique: Kacchi Yakhni Layering & Dough-Sealed Dum Pukht

dishes.name: Hyderabadi Haleem
dishes.description: A GI-tagged royal delicacy: broken whole wheat, lentils, and tender meat pounded continuously with wooden mallets (ghotni) in copper cauldrons for 12 hours until transformed into an intensely rich paste.
dishes.era: Yemeni Chaush Migration & Nizams of Hyderabad
dishes.keyTechnique: 12-Hour Degchi Simmer & Wooden Mallet Pounding

dishes.name: Mui Borok
dishes.description: The traditional staple of the indigenous Borok people: fresh river catch simmered with oil-free berma (sun-dried fermented fish paste), fresh mountain chillies, and indigenous wild leaves.
dishes.keyTechnique: Zero-Oil Earthen Pot Boil with Fermented Berma

dishes.name: Chakhwi
dishes.description: A cherished ceremonial preparation of tender bamboo shoots, pork cuts, and jackfruit seeds simmered in an indigenous natural alkaline extract prepared from burnt bamboo ash.
dishes.keyTechnique: Bamboo Ash Filtration & Forest Root Simmer

dishes.name: Awan Bangwi
dishes.description: Glutinous rice, jaggery and sometimes grated coconut wrapped in banana or turmeric leaf and steam-baked into a fragrant cake; prepared for Tripuri household celebrations and offerings.
dishes.era: Tripuri festival-food tradition; documented in ethnographic accounts
dishes.keyTechnique: Leaf-Wrapped Rice Steaming

dishes.name: Awadhi Galouti Kebab
dishes.description: Legendary melt-in-the-mouth smoked minced meat patties infused with 160 secret botanical aromatics, raw green papaya tenderizer, and pure ghee, originally created for toothless Nawab Asad-ud-Daula.
dishes.keyTechnique: Multiple Sil-Batta Grindings, Smoke Infusion (Dhungar) & Mahi Tawa Griddling

dishes.name: Banarasi Kachori Sabzi
dishes.description: Golden flaky deep-fried breads stuffed with a seasoned paste of black lentils (urad dal) and asafoetida, served on leaf donas with a tart, unpeeled potato curry simmered with whole fenugreek.
dishes.keyTechnique: Deep Immersion Frying & Slow Fenugreek-Hing Potato Tempering

dishes.name: Banarasi Malaiyo
dishes.description: A winter-only Varanasi delicacy: full-fat milk boiled with saffron and sugar, chilled overnight under the dew, then whisked with hand-churned cream into an airy foam dusted with pistachio.
dishes.era: Varanasi winter sweet, documented in 20th-century city food writing
dishes.keyTechnique: Dew-Chilled Milk & Hand-Whisked Cream Foam

dishes.name: Kafuli
dishes.description: A velvety, iron-rich emerald green gravy made of wild mountain spinach and fresh fenugreek leaves slow-cooked in iron pots, thickened with rice flour and tempered in cold-pressed mustard oil with jakhiya seeds.
dishes.keyTechnique: Cast Iron Kadhai Boiling & Wood Churning (Mathani)

dishes.name: Bal Mithai
dishes.description: A GI-tagged chocolate-brown chewy fudge made by roasting pure hill-cow milk khoya and cane sugar for 10 hours until deep caramelization, rolled in tiny white sugar-coated poppy beads.
dishes.era: Early 20th Century (Lala Joga Sah of Almora)
dishes.keyTechnique: 10-Hour Khoya Dark Roasting & Sugar Seed Enrobing

dishes.name: Singori
dishes.description: A cone of sweetened, reduced milk solids (khoya) and coconut, wrapped in a folded malu leaf whose aroma perfumes the sweet; a Garhwali–Kumaoni market delicacy.
dishes.era: Garhwali–Kumaoni sweet-making tradition; documented in regional food writing
dishes.keyTechnique: Khoya Reduction & Malu-Leaf Wrapping

dishes.name: Shorshe Ilish
dishes.description: The undisputed empress of Bengali gastronomy: prized silver Padma/Ganga Hilsa fish gently simmered in a freshly stone-ground paste of pungent black and yellow mustard seeds, green chillies, and raw mustard oil.
dishes.era: Mangalkavya Medieval Bengali Literature (15th Century CE)
dishes.keyTechnique: Shil-Nora Mustard Grinding & Raw Mustard Oil Finish

dishes.name: Mishti Doi
dishes.description: Thick full-cream milk boiled down with date palm jaggery (nolen gur) until reduced to half its volume, seeded with active culture and set slowly in unglazed porous terracotta earthen pots that wick excess moisture.
dishes.keyTechnique: Slow Milk Reduction & Unglazed Terracotta Moisture Wicking

dishes.name: Rosogolla
dishes.description: Spongy balls of fresh chhena kneaded until smooth, poached in light sugar syrup until they swell and cool into a syrup-held sphere; 'Banglar Rasogolla' received a GI tag in 2017.
dishes.keyTechnique: Chhena Kneading & Controlled-Syrup Poaching

dishes.name: Rogan Josh
dishes.description: The crown jewel of the royal 36-course Wazwan feast: tender lamb cuts slow-braised in mustard oil, infused with fennel seed powder (saunf), dried ginger (sonth), and the vivid red essence of ratan jot (alkanet root) and Kashmiri chillies.
dishes.keyTechnique: Ratan Jot Color Extraction & Slow Copper Degchi Braise

dishes.name: Kashmiri Dum Aloo
dishes.description: Pricked baby potatoes deep-fried in mustard oil until crisp, then slow-cooked on dum in a velvety yoghurt sauce intensely flavored with Kashmiri chillies, dried ginger, and fennel with no onion or garlic.
dishes.keyTechnique: Potato Pricking, Deep Crisp Frying & Sealed Curd Dum

dishes.name: Old Delhi Nihari
dishes.description: The legendary pre-dawn breakfast of Old Delhi's Jama Masjid: shank meat and marrow bones slow-simmered in large cauldrons through the cold night with over 50 spices, thickened gently with wheat flour.
dishes.era: Late Mughal Era (Reign of Shah Jahan, 17th Century)
dishes.keyTechnique: Overnight Sealed Cauldron Simmer & Bone Marrow Melt

dishes.name: Chandni Chowk Papdi Chaat
dishes.alternateName: The Symphony of Sweet, Sour & Spice
dishes.description: Crispy whole-wheat papdis layered with boiled potatoes, soft chickpeas, thick whisked sweet yoghurt, tangy date-tamarind chutney, spicy green mint chutney, and roasted cumin chaat masala.
dishes.keyTechnique: Layered Chutney Balance & Fresh Crisp Assembly

dishes.name: Ladakhi Skyu
dishes.description: Traditional handmade whole-wheat dough pinched into tiny thumb-sized hollow bowls, slow-simmered in a rich, warming broth with root potatoes, turnips, wild mountain caraway, and tender meat.
dishes.keyTechnique: Thumb-Indent Pasta Shaping & Sustained Broth Simmer

dishes.name: Gur Gur Cha & Khambir
dishes.description: A restorative high-altitude pairing: brick tea churned vigorously with pure yak butter and rock salt in a wooden chandong cylinder, served alongside thick coal-toasted sourdough hearth bread.
dishes.keyTechnique: Wooden Chandong Piston Churning & Hot Ember Toasting

dishes.name: Andaman Coconut Prawn Curry
dishes.description: Succulent freshly harvested Andaman sea prawns poached gently in thick island coconut cream, mustard seeds, curry leaves, and spicy green chillies.
dishes.keyTechnique: Quick High-Heat Poaching in Fresh Coconut Cream

dishes.name: Island Mud Crab Masala
dishes.description: Wild mangrove mud crabs tossed vigorously in crushed Tellicherry black pepper, shallots, roasted coriander, and fresh tamarind pulp over blazing wood fires.
dishes.keyTechnique: Cast Iron Wok Tossing with Pepper Tempering

dishes.name: Kilanji
dishes.description: A delicate rice-flour crepe from Lakshadweep, cooked thin on a hot griddle and served with coconut milk or a lightly spiced accompaniment.
dishes.era: Lakshadweep household tradition; no securely dated first written reference
dishes.keyTechnique: Fine Rice-Batter Griddle Cooking

dishes.name: Lakshadweep Tuna Curry
dishes.description: Fresh tuna simmered with coconut, curry leaves and local aromatics, reflecting the atoll's close relationship with the Arabian Sea.
dishes.era: Lakshadweep island cooking tradition; no securely dated first written reference
dishes.keyTechnique: Gentle Coconut-Broth Simmer

dishes.name: Pondicherry Fish Curry
dishes.description: Tender ocean catch simmered in coconut milk, fenugreek, tamarind, and a subtle French-influenced aniseed and vadouvan spice bouquet.
dishes.era: French East India Company (17th–18th Century Pondicherry)
dishes.keyTechnique: French Bouquet Garni Fusion with Tamil Tamarind Base

dishes.name: Koli Kari
dishes.description: Rich Franco-Tamil fusion chicken stew prepared with freshly grated nutmeg, cloves, saffron-scented potatoes, and velvety coconut cream.
dishes.era: French Creole Elite Kitchens of White Town
dishes.keyTechnique: Gentle Wine/Cream Style Velouté with Tropical Spices
